benchmark_details.name: Nursing Staff Duty Rosters
benchmark_details.overview: Evaluates models' ability to extract structured schedule data from visual nursing staff duty rosters, including shift types, half-day splits, alternate unit assignments, and staff metadata.

purpose_and_intended_users.goal: Measure how well vision-language models read a dense, icon-based staff planning grid: mapping each cell to its date via a separate header, identifying shift icons via a separate legend, and recording half-day splits, shading and alternate unit assignments as structured records. The results are meant to guide nursing and health services researchers who need staffing data from planning sheets that exist only as printouts or scans.
tasks: date alignment of cells across separate images
purpose_and_intended_users.limitations: 21 rows from one monthly roster of one ward in one facility; results do not transfer automatically to other roster software, layouts or icon sets. Days and shifts are compared by position, so a model that omits a day or splits a cell differently shifts every later field into a mismatch. All fields count equally, so the roughly 30 day and 31 shift entries per row (four fields each) outweigh the four person fields and the year and month. The legend holds 33 icons, of which the ground truth uses 20; `Freier Tag` alone makes up a third of all shifts.
out_of_scope_uses: drawing conclusions about the staff, the ward or the facility
re-identifying staff members or analysing their absences
evaluating general table or handwriting recognition

data.source: One monthly staff planning sheet (PEP, file `04-25_PEP_02-12-01`) for April 2025 from one ward of a Swiss nursing care facility, provided through the INTERSCALE study of the Institute of Nursing Science, University of Basel (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06473051), by the domain experts listed under Authors. The facility is not named. The sheet was segmented by hand into one image per staff member's row; the roster header (dates and weekdays) and the icon legend are separate images.
data.annotation: Ground truths were created by the annotator Maximilian Hindermann, with Ana Maria Leonte and Franziska Zúñiga as domain experts (see Contributors by Role), following the extraction rules in the [prompt file](prompts/prompt.txt).
data.collection_date: Not specified for benchmark collection or digitisation. Source-document dates: The roster covers April 2025.
data.contamination_controls: No held-out private split, training-data audit or other contamination control is documented. Inputs, prompts and ground truths are distributed together in this public repository. Whether any evaluated model saw these materials during training is unknown.

methods: zero-shot structured extraction; each request carries the header image, the legend image and one roster row
structured JSON output requested using the `Schedule` dataclass, with `icon` restricted to the 33 legend names
benchmark default output cap of 98,304 tokens; a test rule can override it and model-specific ceilings can lower it
methodology.calculation:
Every terminal field of the JSON (for example `persons[0].days[4].shifts[0].icon`) is compared between response and ground truth by its path; empty strings count as missing. Values are compared with a rapidfuzz similarity score on their string form, and a field is a match at a score of 0.92 or above.

- TP: both have a value and the score is at least 0.92
- FP and FN: both have a value but the score is below 0.92 (the field counts once as each)
- FP: only the response has a value
- FN: only the ground truth has a value

A `null` icon or alternate unit on both sides counts as nothing. F1 per row is rounded to two decimals. F1 micro sums TP, FP and FN over all rows before computing F1; F1 macro averages the per-row F1. There are no configurable field-selection rules. In schema-configured runs, the shared runner skips unparseable responses, so both F1 aggregates cover only scored rows.
methodology.interpretation: Scores range from 0 to 1; higher is better. Both metrics are dominated by shift-level fields; a low score can come from misaligned dates as much as from misread icons.
methodology.baseline_results:
Model results are available on the [benchmark page](https://rise-services.rise.unibas.ch/benchmarks/p/benchmarks/duty_rosters) and in `results/<date>/<test_id>/` at the repository root. Compare runs with the same prompt, scoring rules and ground-truth revision, and report the number of successfully scored objects alongside the score. No fixed model baseline with a run ID and date is specified here.

Observed across models: mapping cells to dates across the separate header image is the largest source of error. Models also confuse empty cells with `Freier Tag` or assign icons such as `HomeOffice` to them.
methodology.validation: The ground truths were created by the annotator listed under Contributors by Role; no separate second check is recorded. Scoring is deterministic; this scorer has no dedicated test in the repository.
methodology.validity_justification: Field-level F1 reflects the downstream use: each shift becomes a record in a staffing dataset, so a field is either usable or needs correction. Not specified beyond that.

ethical_and_legal_considerations.privacy_and_anonymity: The roster is from April 2025 and covers living people. It was anonymised by the facility before release: neither the images nor the ground truths contain names, staff are identified only by the IDs the INTERSCALE study assigned (the handwritten numbers in the margin), the facility is not named, and the ward label is cropped from the current header image. Each row records a profession group, employment percentage and a month of shifts and absences, including sick days (two rows) and a month of maternity protection (one row).
ethical_and_legal_considerations.consent_procedures: The facility released the anonymised roster for publication through the INTERSCALE study.
ethical_and_legal_considerations.compliance_with_regulations: The roster was anonymised by the facility before release and carries only study IDs, so it contains no personal data that identifies staff. The facility granted its use under CC BY 4.0 through the INTERSCALE study. No separate reuse terms are stated for the ground truths. No separate ethical review for the benchmark was carried out.
